newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO-Israeli talks on Hebron resume in Jericho.
newsitem.headline: PLO-Israeli talks on Hebron resume in Jericho.

text.p: Palestinian and Israeli negotiators scheduled talks in self-ruled Jericho for Sunday night to try to sew up a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from the Arab West Bank town of Hebron, PLO officials said.
The last round of talks on Thursday, attended by U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk, failed to bring the sides closer together on the issue.
PLO officials said the talks failed to achieve results because of Israel's insistence its soldiers be allowed to re-enter the 80 percent of the city due to be handed over to the PLO.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has rejected any renegotiation of the Hebron accord signed by the left-centre Israeli government which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ousted in May.
Netanyahu seeks to alter the Hebron accord, maintaining it fails to adequately protect some 400 Jewish settlers who live and study among the more than 100,000 Palestinians of the town.
Under the interim PLO-Israel peace deal, Hebron was to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule last year, but Israel delayed the transfer for security reasons.

"If Israel does not give up asking for the right to re-enter Palestinian areas after handing them over to us, then we will not have an agreement," said one senior PLO security official. "Their demand is a violaiton of our jurisdiction and powers on our territories."
